_headline: DISCLOSURE RUNS UPWARD, NOT DOWNWARD. Two EU instruments have been followed to the national boundary and neither names a member-state publication (Annex XI, Annex B — both recorded as _dropped in eu-draft-budget.json). But member-state documents DO name the EU instrument: two German inventories each state they compile GDP/GNI 'in compliance with' ESA 2010, which is an obligation and not Research.1.md 5a agreement language. The asymmetry is the result — the supranational layer does not name its inputs, and the national layer does name its obligations.
_open_questions: CADENCE for the two Destatis inventories is not stated by either document, so neither is minted — see the no-node-yet entries. Evidence exists for a five-year cycle (HERP benchmark revisions at reference years ending 0/5 and implementation years ending 4/9; 'most recent major revision took place in 2024, and the next is scheduled for 2029'; 'Eurostat GNI verification cycle 2020 to 2024') but that is the REVISION cycle, not a stated publication cadence for the inventories, and the two inventories in hand are Edition 2025 and Edition 2024 — one year apart, which the five-year reading does not explain. Deliberately not guessed: ISSAI 300/400 were refused on the same ground in eu-draft-budget.json and consistency is worth more here than one extra node.

ESA 2010's releases_per_year of 0.05 mirrors sna-2008 exactly (also 0.05, also a generational standard). Observed ESA intervals are shorter than that implies — ESA 1995 to ESA 2010 is 15 years, and a further revision is already named in an ESAC opinion ('the revised European System of Accounts (ESA) in line with the newly endorsed System of National Accounts (SNA 2025)'). 0.067 would fit the observed intervals better. Matched to the corpus precedent rather than the arithmetic; flag if the precedent is the thing that is wrong.

reports.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
reports.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

reports.title: ESA 2010 Methods and Sources for the German GNI (Gross National Income) and Its Components
reports.description: Destatis's own detailed inventory of the methods and sources used to compile Germany's GDP and GNI 'in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010'. Its own colophon states 'Periodicity: non-recurring', Research.1.md 4.2's exact one-off disqualifier -- but the same document has a section headed 'Revisions policy and major revisions since the 2021 inventory', and the landing page's 'Older editions' heading links a 2016 edition, so at minimum three editions demonstrably exist (2016, 2021, 2025 -- current edition, published 12 March 2026). Minted as a regular node 2026-08-08 on Thomas's ruling (Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx Q2): treat 'non-recurring' as a per-publication metadata label rather than a hard disqualifier, and estimate a cadence from the observed interval for the pulse animation.
reports.cadence_note: ESTIMATED, not stated: the document's own colophon says 'Periodicity: non-recurring' and names no publication schedule. The 2021-to-2025 gap between its own cited predecessor and the current edition is the only observed interval (4 years, releases_per_year 0.25); the landing page's separate 2016 edition is noted but not used for the estimate, since the 2016-to-2021 gap (5 years) and 2021-to-2025 gap (4 years) are not the same length and this project does not average intervals from different revision regimes without evidence they are the same cycle. Per Thomas's Q2 ruling this is an estimate for the pulse visualisation, not a documented cadence.

release_schedule.note: Destatis's ESA 2010 Methods and Sources page shows only two editions on record: 'Edition 2016' (previous) and 'Edition 2025' (current, dated 12 March 2026). No release calendar, no stated periodicity rule, and no consistent multi-point pattern was found (only two data points, ~9 years apart). This document is Germany's GNI Inventory required for EU 'own resources' GNI verification; such inventories are typically revised/updated when the European Commission's GNI Committee runs a verification cycle, which occurs at irregular multi-year intervals rather than a fixed schedule. releases_per_year=0.25 (implying a 4-year cycle) does not match the observed ~9-year gap between the only two known editions.

reports.title: Quarterly National Accounts Inventory Based on ESA 2010 Methodology
reports.description: Destatis's companion inventory for the quarterly national accounts, stating it 'contains the detailed description of the quarterly methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product of Germany in compliance with the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)' and that 'the structure of the description follows a uniform European standard that was developed by the Statistical Office of the European Communities'. Current edition dated 12 September 2024 ('Edition 2024'); an earlier, differently-numbered publication in the same territory (Fachserie 18 Reihe S.31, 'Edition 2017') is marked as its own series' last issue and may or may not be a true predecessor to the present standalone document -- not confirmed either way. Minted as a regular node 2026-08-08 on Thomas's ruling (Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx Q2), same as the GNI inventory.
reports.cadence_note: ESTIMATED, not stated: unlike the GNI inventory, this document carries no periodicity statement at all and names no confirmed predecessor edition -- the Fachserie 18 Reihe S.31 'last issue' (2017) found this session may be an unrelated, discontinued series rather than a true predecessor, and that was not run to ground. The 0.25 estimate is carried over from the GNI inventory's demonstrated interval on the reasoning that both inventories sit under the same Eurostat GNI-verification-style revision cycle, per Thomas's instruction to estimate for the pulse visualisation -- flagged as the weaker of the two estimates in this file.

release_schedule.note: The document is a methodological 'inventory' describing sources and methods for German Quarterly National Accounts under ESA 2010, published as numbered editions (current: 'Edition 2024', dated 12 September 2024). Neither the PDF itself nor the surrounding Destatis publication pages state an update frequency, edition history, or next planned release date. It appears to be revised irregularly, as needed when compilation methodology changes, rather than on a fixed schedule -- analogous to other EU member states' ESA 2010 national-accounts-inventory documents submitted to Eurostat, which are updated on an as-needed basis rather than a calendar.

dependencies.basis: The inventory states its own legal basis twice, in obligation and derivation language rather than 5a agreement language: 'The present document contains the detailed description of the methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product and the gross national income of the Federal Republic of Germany in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010', and 'describes the methods and statistical sources used to calculate GDP and GNI at market prices for the Federal Republic of Germany based on the European System of Accounts (ESA) 2010'. 'In compliance with' and 'based on' name ESA 2010 as the rulebook the inventory's own compilation follows, the same relationship already established from the release side by de-destatis-national-accounts -> esa-2010.

'The present document contains the detailed description of the quarterly methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product of Germany in compliance with the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010).' A second sentence in the same document adds a further, distinct dependency not modelled as its own edge here: 'The structure of the description follows a uniform European standard that was developed by the Statistical Office of the European Communities' -- the inventory's own STRUCTURE, not just its content, is set by Eurostat.

_dropped.why: A PREDICTED EDGE, REFUTED BY Research.1.md 5a. ESA 2010's own text says: 'The ESA 2010 is consistent with the worldwide guidelines on national accounting set out in the System of National Accounts 2008 (2008 SNA)' (Annex A, Chapter 1, paragraph 1.05). 'Consistent with' is verbatim on 5a's watchlist and is agreement between two frameworks, not derivation of one from the other. Two further records say it the same way and were already flagged by the original extractor: the supply-and-use manual — 'The ESA 1995 is fully consistent with the world-wide System of National Accounts (SNA 1993)' — and Eurostat's national accounts page — 'This system is fully consistent with the worldwide guidelines on national accounting, the System of national accounts (SNA).' Three independent statements, all agreement language, none a dependency. Per 5a this is worth recording precisely because the link is plausible enough to be re-proposed every few months; it was re-proposed this session.

THE BEST CROSS-LAYER CANDIDATE FOUND SO FAR, and the direction is the surprise. Destatis: 'The present document contains the detailed description of the methods and sources used for the compilation of the gross domestic product and the gross national income of the Federal Republic of Germany in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010.' A second record from the same document: 'describes the methods and statistical sources used to calculate GDP and GNI at market prices for the Federal Republic of Germany based on the European System of Accounts (ESA) 2010.' 'In compliance with' and 'based on' are obligation and derivation language, NOT 5a agreement language — a real methodology_depends_on running from a member-state publication to the EU instrument. NOT MINTED, and the cadence question was looked up on 2026-08-05 rather than left open. THE ANSWER IS A DOCUMENTED CONFLICT, reported per 3 and not adjudicated. The publication's own colophon states 'Periodicity: non-recurring' (Statistisches Bundesamt, published March 2026), which is Research.1.md 4.2's exact disqualifier — 'something published once is not a node'. But the SAME DOCUMENT names its own predecessor: section 1.2 is headed 'Revisions policy and major revisions since the 2021 inventory', and the Destatis landing page carries an 'Older editions' heading. So a 2021 edition and a 2025 edition demonstrably exist, four years apart, consistent with the Eurostat GNI verification cycle documented elsewhere in the corpus ('Eurostat action points from the GNI verification cycle 2020 to 2024'). Reading: 'non-recurring' is most likely a per-publication metadata label meaning 'not a scheduled series release' rather than a claim that no further inventory will appear — but that is an inference about what the publisher meant, and 6 says do not guess a cadence to make the JSON validate. If the other end of the process reads 'non-recurring' as a metadata artefact, releases_per_year 0.25 is the number the observed 2021->2025 interval supports.

_dropped.edge: esa-2010 -> any named member-state statistical release
_dropped.why: A corpus observation carried here so it sits next to the node it concerns. ESA 2010 obliges transmission but names no member-state publication: Annex B is 'a programme setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit the accounts and tables', its table overview has four columns (number, subject, deadline, period) and no column for a publication, and Destatis describing its own transmission names ten ESA table numbers and no German publication. Combined with the Annex XI salary chain, that is two independent binding instruments stopping at AGENCY ONLY at the national boundary. Both are recorded in full in eu-draft-budget.json's _dropped list; full assessments in EU/AnnexB_assessment_2026-08-05.md and EU/AnnexXI_PartA_2026-08-05.md. Read against the two no-node-yet entries above, which run the other way and do name their target.

NEW LEAD, opened 2026-08-05 while closing the inventory cadence question, and it looks more promising than either inventory. The inventories are METHODOLOGY documents whose cadence is contested; the RELEASE they describe has a documented timetable: 'First quarterly results of GDP without particular breakdown are published as press release 30 days after the end of a reporting quarter. The more detailed figures are published around 55 days after the end of the reporting quarter.' That is a stated quarterly cadence, which is what 4.2 wants, and the transmission record ties it to the EU instrument: 'The German QNA are transmitted to Eurostat in accordance with the mandatory ESA transmission program.' Two things are missing before it can be minted: an exact published TITLE for the release (the records call it 'the German QNA', a category rather than a title — 4.3), and its own URL, distinct from the inventory PDF that describes it. Both are one Destatis lookup away.
